svg.title: Memory corpus commit and crash recovery
svg.desc: A multi-file memory corpus write stages new and old bytes, writes a journal atomically, replaces each member with MEMORY.md last, records the manifest and cleans up. After a crash, recovery compares the MEMORY.md revision with the journal target: equal rolls forward from the stage files, otherwise it rolls back from the backups. A missing backup or a corpus that does not verify raises MemoryCorpusRecoveryRequired and the corpus stays unavailable.

g.text: Hover a step for what it writes and what a crash there leaves behind; its connections light up. Click it to open its section.
Inside a rendered document this image is static. Click it to open the interactive SVG.

svg.text: Memory corpus commit and crash recovery
A multi-file write is journaled; MEMORY.md is replaced last, so its revision tells recovery which way to go.

g.text: COMMIT · MemoryCorpusService, UNDER THE WORKSPACE LOCK

g.class: e bad dash f-journal f-replace f-manifest f-cleanup t-found
g.text: crash after step 2: recovery runs at the next access
an error in steps 1 to 5 runs it at once, then rethrows
stage · every changed member is written to stage-N and its current bytes to backup-N, inside .dartclaw-memory-transaction/
An earlier transaction directory is deleted first. Nothing in the corpus has changed, so a crash here needs no recovery; the next write cleans up.
journal · written atomically only after every stage and backup file exists: collectionId, base and target revision and fingerprint, entries
Its presence is what makes recovery run after a crash. Before it exists there is nothing to roll either way.
replace · each changed member is replaced from its stage file, MEMORY.md last
MEMORY.md carries a Collection-Revision line, so a reader that sees the target revision there knows every other member was already replaced.
manifest · the manifest is rewritten after the members: revision, fingerprint, member digests and record ids
Coordination state only: a missing manifest is rebuilt from the Markdown.
cleanup · _cleanupTransaction removes the journal and the transaction directory; the post-commit hook then re-projects the committed entries
A hook failure marks the derived index degraded and leaves canonical memory available.
journal found? · _recoverLocked returns at once when the journal file is absent
It runs first in every manifest preparation, authenticate and write, and in-process when a commit throws, before the original error is rethrown.
MEMORY.md revision · the commit-marker test: the Collection-Revision prefix of MEMORY.md against the journal target
Step 3 replaced MEMORY.md last, so equality proves every other member was already replaced; anything else is treated as not committed.
roll forward · committed: copy every entry from its stage file again, then verify against the journal target
Replaying is idempotent, so a crash during recovery is recovered the same way on the next access.
roll back · not committed: restore entries in reverse order from backup-N, or delete the file when it was a new member
A missing backup raises MemoryCorpusRecoveryRequired. A base revision of 0 (the first commit) just cleans up, with no verification.
verify and rewrite manifest · recomputes member descriptors and compares collectionId and fingerprint with the journal
Then it rewrites the manifest and cleans up. A MEMORY.md revision matching neither side, or an identity mismatch, throws; nothing is guessed.
the corpus stays unavailable; other workspaces are unaffected
MemoryCorpusRecoveryRequired · raised for a missing backup, a revision matching neither side, or an identity or fingerprint mismatch
Startup authenticates each corpus in bounded batches; a failed corpus stays unavailable without affecting the owner or other workspaces.
